release: CoreSpirit v64 — six-concept language surface over the converged v1 runtime
runtime_baseline: v63 unified language surface, v62 visual coordinates, v61 converged v1 runtime
focus: six semantic user concepts: DATA, LET, WHEN, SHOW, MODEL and AUTOMATE
WHEN indentation/colon syntax lowers to the existing if control-flow ABI
quoted WHEN event names lower to host-resolved event queries
SHOW multi-value and area forms lower to the existing plot/scene placement contract
MODEL and AUTOMATE declarations become stable metadata on the same executable artifact
no second AST, parser, evaluator, model runtime or broker execution path
host-owned event input remains explicit and replayable
editor presents the six concepts as the primary source-language vocabulary
architecture_invariants: the user mental model has six semantic concepts, not a list of subsystem-specific functions
the executable parser remains the existing small grammar
WHEN and SHOW are source conveniences that lower into existing semantics
MODEL/AUTOMATE declarations are serializable metadata on the same executable artifact
incoming automation events are host-supplied and cannot become broker authority
MODEL remains behind the strict host-owned model ABI
AUTOMATE remains behind order-intent, risk, policy and host execution boundaries
all six concepts use the same AST, stable IR and VM
surface semantics never grant host capabilities
CORESPIRIT.md remains the stable architecture brain
CORESPIRIT_BUILD_TRACKER.md remains the living implementation truth
CORESPIRIT_Vxx_MANIFEST.json remains the machine release record
